title: Focus the next service on self-served B2C
content: The team decided that the next service should focus on B2C rather than B2B or enterprise customers, with every part of the product delivered through a self-served model.

title: The next service needs a clear north-star metric
content: The team identified the absence of a clear north-star metric as an unresolved issue for the next service.

title: Research U.S. finance, accounting, and Excel-heavy workflows
content: The team needs to investigate how finance and accounting work in the United States, which roles use Excel most often, whether those workflows are sufficiently difficult or frequent for AI assistance, the size of each field, and whether data analysis is the best opportunity.

title: Adopt the vision Unlock human minds, seamlessly
content: The vision selected for the new product direction is: Unlock human minds, seamlessly.

title: Do not build the new Excel product on top of inline AI
content: The team decided to start the new Excel product from scratch rather than add it to inline AI because interviewed Excel users generally had no prior inline AI usage and the existing inline AI customer base was not the intended target audience.

title: Keep existing products running without prioritizing a sale
content: The team determined that selling inline AI or the student-record product was not central to the company's direction. The student-record product would remain listed, while the other existing services would be maintained without customer support and otherwise deprioritized.

title: Target the U.S. Excel workflow market with a new product
content: The team chose the United States as the target market and Excel as the target tool. The initial workflow is Raw Data -> Data Cleansing -> Data Analysis -> Report or Dashboard, with the workflow and tool taking precedence over selecting a narrow consumer persona.

title: Chang-sik to learn the Claude API and agent development stack
content: Chang-sik will study the existing code and API structure through the Claude API documentation, use Claude Code during the work to learn its structure and workflow, review the agent development references, and watch the AI Engineer course materials.

title: Sang-yeon to conduct Excel user research
content: Sang-yeon will investigate relevant Reddit communities and schedule an interview about Excel use.

title: Sang-yeon to define the PO role and write a business one-pager
content: Sang-yeon will define the product owner role and prepare a one-page business strategy document.

title: Poetry setup hit WinError 193 on Windows
content: Chang-sik encountered WinError 193, stating that the target is not a valid Win32 application, while setting up Poetry.

title: Establish the Electron and agent architecture by January 30
content: The team planned to establish the Electron application and core agent architecture by January 30, including agent execution, context management, human-in-the-loop controls, process communication, testing, development logs, and a written specification.

title: Implement authentication, billing, and local file search in February
content: The roadmap called for selecting and implementing authentication around February 3, researching local file search and extension-specific readers by February 9, and building Paddle-based subscription and credit billing after the payment policy was finalized.

title: Combine Excel editing with local file search and context
content: The initial product direction combined the planned Excel agent with local file search and opening, web search, and contextual use of PDF, Word, and other files. Editing would remain focused on Excel while other formats would supply context.

title: Define Cicely AI as a desktop-native AI coworker
content: The long-term product vision was set as an AI coworker that lives on the user's computer. The initial delivery was defined as a desktop-native AI coworker for Excel.

title: Make autonomy, observability, teamwork, and auditability core agent principles
content: The agent was required to act autonomously while communicating its progress, support human-in-the-loop questions and tool approval, and provide checkpoints and reversion so its work could be trusted and audited.

title: Name the product cicely.ai
content: After comparing the final candidates against pronunciation, search uniqueness, domain availability, keyword competition, autocomplete, and trademark criteria, the team selected cicely.ai as the product name.

title: Set a 90 percent payment-retention target and June revenue goal
content: The north-star targets were 90 percent payment retention and USD 1 million in MRR by June, supported by targets of 25,000 subscribers, 500,000 sign-ups, and 5 million visitors.

title: Target the United States while publishing SEO content in both languages
content: The team decided to target only the United States for the product while continuing to publish SEO content in both Korean and English.

title: Target white-collar workers who use Excel every day
content: The team chose general white-collar workers who use Excel daily, including FP&A, operations, data analysis, managerial accounting, and finance, rather than limiting the initial target to Excel power users or a single profession.

title: Use a self-served product-led go-to-market strategy
content: The team decided to remain self-served and product-driven, develop through a consumer feedback loop and building in public, and avoid custom feature work, outbound sales, and prematurely selling bespoke implementations.

title: Cicely AI premortem identified retention, distribution, reliability, and UX risks
content: The premortem highlighted four major failure modes: daily Excel users may not need AI daily, organic distribution may fail, version differences or agent loops may corrupt work, and the product may feel too complex or less appealing than fully autonomous workers.

title: Local-file telemetry creates a serious privacy risk
content: The logging plan identified company spreadsheets and original files as particularly sensitive. Product analytics, agent traces, prompts, and failures were needed, but any file collection required an explicit mode, limited sampling, or structured XML rather than indiscriminate upload.

title: Build agent and Excel evaluation systems with small batches
content: The team will build agent and Excel evaluation systems using unit-test-style checks and start with small evaluation batches before scaling them up.

title: Design payment, authentication, and settings before the main UX
content: The team will ask 성현 to design the payment, authentication, and settings flows by February 9, then implement the main chat and agent UX as a functional skeleton before polishing the UI.

title: Prepare marketing and launch operations before payment ships
content: The team will begin email marketing and CRM preparation before the payment system is finished, and will also prepare the website, demo video, build-in-public activity, customer-support channel, and QA sheet.

title: Design the Excel agent for multi-workbook use from the start
content: The team divided agent development into single-workbook Excel problem solving, multi-workbook integration and workflow automation, and local file search, and decided to account for multi-workbook support from the initial architecture.

title: Manage Cicely AI Version 1 as a Linear initiative
content: The team decided to use Linear's timeline view, make Building Cicely AI Version 1 the top-level initiative, organize the work into child projects, and use milestones to group project work.

title: Protect original files with checkpoints and revert support
content: The proposed Cicely AI UX would provide checkpoints and file-backup-based revert behavior while guiding operations toward a flow that does not modify the original file directly.

title: Cicely AI Version 1 delivery plan targets February 27
content: The Cicely AI Version 1 plan set February 27 as the final target, with local file search targeted for February 8, payment and UI work in February, roughly two weeks of QA, and beta distribution in the final week.

title: Complete the initial environment setup by Thursday
content: The team will complete the initial development environment by Thursday, then implement local file search and web search and review the remaining AI-agent issues.

title: Investigate active Excel communities and creator outreach
content: The team will investigate and join active Excel-related Discord servers and contact the identified YouTube creator who publishes Excel content.

title: Start audience discovery and interaction on X and Reddit
content: The team will begin identifying the target audience on X and Reddit, participate through comments and discussions, and continuously collect complaints and needs rather than treating the work as one-way content publishing.

title: Defer Langfuse integration until the production environment
content: The team decided that Langfuse tracing could be postponed until the production environment was being built because it was not required for the immediate implementation and improvement work.

title: Focus community work on X, Reddit, and existing Discord servers
content: The team selected X and Reddit as the primary channels, deprioritized LinkedIn and Threads, and chose to join active Excel-related Discord communities instead of creating a new Discord server immediately.

title: Prioritize local search, web search, authentication, payments, and LLM request design
content: The development sequence was set as initial environment setup, local file search, web search, DDD-based authentication and payment systems, and LLM request design. The backend migration to C3 was also part of this plan.

title: Use founder profiles for build-in-public marketing before paid influencers
content: The team decided that paid influencer marketing was premature. Sang-yeon and Chang-sik will participate in communities through their personal profiles, build trust through authentic two-way interaction, learn user pain points, and introduce Cicely AI only after establishing credibility.

title: Cicely AI homepage and demo were targeted for mid-to-late February
content: The homepage and product demo were expected in mid-to-late February. Until then, community participation and social engagement were prioritized over collecting a waitlist.

title: Connect product telemetry and lifecycle messaging
content: The team will connect Mixpanel user events, Langfuse LLM traces and prompts, error logging, email CRM, Loops, ChannelTalk, and Contact Us before launch.

title: Define user flows for 429 and 402 payment errors
content: The team will implement UX for 429 usage-limit errors with a subscription nudge, and for 402 payment failures with guidance to change the payment method or move to the free plan.

title: Finish the Cicely Version 1 build before QA and release
content: The team planned to finish UI and UX, agent evaluation changes, settings and preferences, payment-limit handling, build and auto-update work, and telemetry by Friday, then run QA and target release the following week.

title: Split ownership between QA and distribution
content: 찬용 will prepare the QA sheet and verify agent-cancellation UX, while 이상연 will divide time equally between evaluation work and distribution after finishing the remaining UI and UX work.

title: Inject saved preferences from the backend
content: The backend will retrieve each user's saved preferences and combine them with the system prompt for LLM calls, using a flow similar to the initial user status loaded at the start of a cycle.

title: Track usage by frontend-generated cycle IDs
content: The new usage model uses a cycle ID generated by the frontend and required by every metered API call. Usage Records track cycle state, cost, refunds, and total usage, while Call Records track individual request IDs.

title: Distribution is the largest launch uncertainty
content: The team identified distribution as the least certain part of the launch. The beta goal was 100 testers, but only about six had been secured, and the team lacked confidence about channels and advertising budget.

title: Delegate local file exploration to a specialized subagent
content: The team documented a proposal for an orchestrator to delegate local file discovery to a local_file_explorer subagent, which would use restricted local paths, return a structured Markdown report with references, and keep its internal context separate from the main agent.

title: Store agent memories as hidden Markdown files
content: The team proposed turning the unused Write or Take Note tool into a background Write Memory tool that stores durable discoveries, preferences, and work patterns in Markdown without rendering them in the UI. The same approach could move highly specific instructions out of a system prompt that currently exceeds 30,000 tokens.

title: MRR reached KRW 20.2 million including B2B
content: The team reported monthly recurring revenue of KRW 20.2 million when B2B revenue was included.

title: Build launch assets and recruit 100 beta testers
content: The distribution plan is to build and polish the website, produce a promotional video and a single guide video covering about four use cases, recruit 100 beta testers, and test ads, lead generation, and cold email.

title: Define Mixpanel events across the full product journey
content: The product analytics plan covers app and authentication events, document pairing, messaging and streaming, navigation, uploads and citations, subscription and credit behavior, invitations, mode changes, HWP compatibility alerts, restart actions, tool execution, and HITL approvals. Message history remains stored in MongoDB.

title: Differentiate inline AI through interactive in-place document editing
content: inline AI should be presented as editing the document that is already open instead of repeatedly generating new files. Users can watch changes, give feedback, and finish long structured reports, proposals, and plans with greater confidence in the final deliverable.

title: Make local processing and data non-retention core privacy claims
content: The privacy message for inline AI is that chat history and the application's core code and logic stay on the user's computer, files are processed locally instead of uploaded for server-side preprocessing, and prompts sent to OpenAI or Anthropic are covered by Zero Data Retention and deleted after processing.

title: Position inline AI as a local AI coworker for professionals
content: The chosen positioning for inline AI is a local AI assistant, or AI coworker, for professionals that can work autonomously while remaining controllable by the user.

title: Documented inline AI file support as of March 29, 2026
content: inline AI can find, open, read, edit, and finish files on the user's computer. The documented readable formats are XLSX, XLSM, XLTX, XLTM, XLS, XLSB, PPTX, PPT, DOCX, PDF, CSV, PNG, JPG, JPEG, HWP, and HWPX. The editable formats are the Excel variants plus HWP and HWPX, with PPT and Word editing planned later.

title: One inline AI conversation can control multiple documents
content: inline AI can recognize and work across multiple open HWP and Excel documents in one conversation, unlike document-scoped assistants such as Microsoft Copilot or Claude for Excel.

title: inline AI supports three validated AI model options
content: As of March 29, 2026, the documented supported models were GPT-5.4, Claude Sonnet 4.6, and Claude Opus 4.6. Before releasing a model integration, the team runs quantitative and qualitative tests on 700 Excel files and 300 HWP documents.

title: Buy a Windows laptop for on-premises development
content: The team plans to purchase a Windows laptop in the KRW 2-3 million range for on-premises installation and development work.

title: Complete the second stabilization pass by April 24
content: The second stabilization pass is targeted for April 24 and should prioritize the missing-font problem, repeated updater behavior, application shutdown during startup or navigation, and review of recurring-payment failure handling; lower-priority enhancements were moved to a later backlog.

title: Finish and deploy the website and analytics foundation by April 21
content: By April 21, the team planned to finish and deploy the website, connect GA4 and GTM, implement the one-time mobile-link email, and prepare the rebranding announcement for the blog channel.

title: Run eight sales meetings from April 22 through April 24
content: Two team members will split eight scheduled sales meetings evenly. Each meeting should demonstrate inline AI, explain the team plan and relevant use cases, and offer 10,000 additional credits when the customer permits recording for possible content use.

title: Do not add credit rollover or standalone credit purchases
content: The team decided not to add credit rollover. Standalone credit purchases and pay-after-the-fact billing were deferred because they did not fit the current tiered subscription model.

title: Limit the next team-plan release to invitation acceptance
content: The team decided to finish the flow in which an invited user can accept inside the app after the organization is created. Notifications should work while the app is open and persist so the invitation remains available when the app is reopened; broader onboarding automation was deferred.

title: Proceed with the IITP model-hosting and agent project for KRW 350 million
content: The team decided to proceed with the IITP project for KRW 350 million including VAT. The scope includes hosting Gemma and EXAONE 4.5, deploying the agent service, initially running on H100 hardware, porting to H200 later, and supporting model updates for one year.

title: Remove time-based proration from subscription upgrades
content: For an upgrade, the customer will pay only the price difference between plans and receive the corresponding increase in plan credits. The existing billing-cycle end date remains unchanged, so payment and added credits are no longer scaled by the number of days remaining in the cycle.

title: Simplify CRM to one-time transactional emails
content: The team removed complex lifecycle sequences. A user should receive a single email at signup, and a mobile download-link request should trigger one immediate email; longer sequences can be reconsidered after the user guide exists.

title: Start paid acquisition with KRW 1 million in Google Ads
content: The initial paid advertising plan is to spend KRW 1 million on Google Ads, focusing on Excel-oriented professional audiences before increasing the budget based on observed performance.

title: IITP project structure could hide inline AI and reduce strategic value
content: The IITP paperwork and security-review structure remained unresolved. The team was concerned that an anonymous SI-style delivery could prevent inline AI and the company name from benefiting from the security review and could weaken the opportunity to package the work as a reusable on-premises solution.

title: Build SEO acquisition assets and an HWP-to-Markdown converter
content: The team will create an automated blog publishing system, finish polishing the existing blog, and add a Hancom Hangul (HWP)-to-Markdown converter to the website as an acquisition tool.

title: Chang-sik to stabilize HWP and Excel processes
content: Chang-sik will consolidate Hancom Hangul (HWP) work into one process with a globally managed instance and investigate the Excel freezing behavior as part of system stabilization.

title: Evaluate HWP performance with an additional open-source model
content: Chang-sik will integrate an additional open-source model for speed and cost efficiency. Sang-yeon will expand the HWP evaluation set and measure correct placement, preservation of unchanged content, writing quality, price, and speed.

title: Improve product education and website credibility
content: The team will add references from brands currently using the product, write user documentation, and produce a guide video for users who do not know how to use the service.

title: Launch Google paid ads and direct influencer advertising
content: The business plan called for starting Google paid advertising and directly approaching roughly three influencers for advertising rather than using an agency.

title: Sang-yeon to fix incorrect placement in HWP edit test 14
content: Sang-yeon will investigate and fix the read and edit problem in test case 14, where content is inserted into the wrong location in a complex HWP table.

title: Set up product analytics and analyze non-converting conversations
content: The team will configure inline AI tracking and Mixpanel, define the metrics to observe, and review conversations from free users who did not convert and subscribers who churned.

title: Defer B2B enablement materials and lower-priority HWP features
content: The team deferred the B2B usage estimator, admin-page entry changes, downloadable sales collateral, additional Markdown and text-file support, and advanced HWP formatting until the product, model, and cost structure were more stable.

title: Introduce a KRW 50,000 bug bounty for actionable reports
content: The team decided to pay KRW 50,000 for a successful, reproducible bug report and add a dedicated bug-report form that can collect details and files, with an NDA included when needed.

title: Prioritize B2C internally instead of enterprise
content: The team decided to place its immediate internal focus on B2C because concentrating on enterprise would require additional concerns such as on-premises deployment and uncertain local-model performance.

title: The June 30 MRR target was KRW 1.5 billion
content: The team stated a target of reaching KRW 1.5 billion in monthly recurring revenue by June 30, which represented roughly 50-fold growth from the current level.

title: Build Python execution skills for five document formats
content: The team will build a controlled Python execution environment and detailed skills for Word, HWP, Excel, PowerPoint, and PDF.

title: Build the fast-processing and memory MVP in two weeks
content: The team committed to a two-week MVP that lets users complete repeated office work quickly and re-run a previously created workflow more cheaply and efficiently.

title: Expose saved workflows through commands and previews
content: The team will let users recall saved prompts or workflows with slash commands in the composer, show frequent skills as home-screen buttons, display scripts and workflows in a list with previews, and provide input fields for variable values.

title: Make workflow credit savings visible
content: The product should clearly show credit usage and explain that saving a workflow reduces the cost and time of later executions.

title: Provide built-in document converters
content: The team will provide built-in converters for common document-format transformations instead of requiring users to install external libraries themselves.

title: Position the product as AI for fast office-work execution
content: The team decided to position the product as an automation AI that quickly handles office and document work across a user's computer, rather than limiting the product to document writing alone.

title: Prioritize fast document execution plus memory
content: The team identified two user needs: deeply refining a valuable document through interaction and quickly completing repetitive short documents, transformations, or office tasks. The current priority is the fast, programmatic execution path combined with memory.

title: Reuse saved scripts by separating code from inputs
content: Repeated workflows should save a generated Python script separately from its variable inputs, so later runs can extract new values and execute the existing script instead of regenerating the entire implementation.

title: Separate user preferences from dynamic workflow memory
content: The memory architecture should keep stable user preferences such as fonts, tone, bullet style, and document structure separate from dynamic memories such as reusable scripts and project- or document-specific context.

title: Users do not know how to use the current service
content: Users reported that they did not know how to use the service and could not find adequate guidance or training.

title: Complete DOCX editing by the third week of June
content: Sangyeon is responsible for entering Word development after the HWP refactor and completing DOCX editing functionality by the third week of June.

title: Implement daily credits for free users
content: Changshik will implement a daily-credit system so free users can return and use the product within a limited daily allowance.

title: Build a standards-compatible Create Skill system
content: The product should include built-in skills and a Create Skill capability for user-defined automation. The skill structure should follow the international agent-skill standard discussed in the meeting, remain compatible with Claude-style skills where possible, and distinguish public skills from private internal capabilities.

title: Focus code execution on office-work operations outside existing document editing
content: The team decided to preserve its high-quality COM-based document editing and use the new code-execution environment primarily for PDF and image generation, local-file operations, text extraction, and other steps that occur before or around editing rather than duplicating the existing editor.

title: Prioritize distribution and Word before expanding to PPT
content: The team chose distribution and format expansion as the main focus, with Word development first. PPT work should not expand the scope prematurely, and file-format conversion was excluded from the immediate iteration discussed at the start of the meeting.

title: Run arbitrary code in disposable server-side sandboxes
content: The team chose a VM or container architecture in which generated code runs on the server rather than directly on the user's computer. A desktop session exposes the local working folder through a mounted connection, dependencies can be preinstalled in the sandbox, and server-side working data should be deleted after the task to reduce security and privacy risk.

title: Target 100,000 active users by September 30
content: The team set September 30 as the deadline for reaching 100,000 active users and chose user growth as the single company-level objective. The meeting summary labels the metric MAU, while an appended planning section labels the same 100,000 target WAU; the source does not resolve the discrepancy.

title: Unify prompt memory and custom automation under Skills
content: The team decided to present prompt memory and custom automation as one user-facing Skills concept. Skills should be invokable with slash commands, and the UI can offer prompts such as 'Would you like to automate this task?' without exposing implementation details.

title: User-uploaded files must be handled carefully in internal testing
content: The team identified a privacy risk in describing or performing tests with files uploaded by users. Even when files were voluntarily submitted, internal testing and external explanations must avoid implying unrestricted use of personal customer data.

title: Finish Skill, Word, Stripe, and QA in sequence
content: The near-term plan is to finish Skill details during the current week, complete Word as soon as possible, add Stripe the following week, and use the next week for QA before release.

title: Run a Cursor Cloud Agent and Linear automation PoC
content: The team will first test a native Cursor Cloud Agent and Linear workflow in which custom Linear statuses trigger planning and implementation. If native integration cannot preserve one continuous thread, the team will consider an SDK-based approach with managed session IDs.

title: Validate the professional-firm ICP through direct outreach
content: The team will interview and demo to executives at small professional firms through LinkedIn and Korean professional networks, and will ask 김동신 for introductions to relevant target customers.

title: Launch Workspace on one high-memory server first
content: For launch speed, Workspace will initially run on one high-memory server. After usage grows, the infrastructure should move to multiple machines with Redis tracking which machine owns each user's session.

title: Position inline AI as an AI-native work system
content: The team chose an AI-native positioning: all relevant context should be readable by AI, and the AI should perform real professional work to output quality rather than merely automate a narrow workflow or generate a one-way draft.

title: Start with individual professionals and expand to teams
content: The initial ICP is individual professionals and 1-to-10-person professional firms such as accounting, legal, and sales teams. The product should first make one professional more capable, then expand naturally into shared team memory and alignment, with the United States as the primary market.

title: Target July 3 for the Word, Workspace, Skill, and Stripe release
content: The release target was set for July 3 with Word, Workspace, inline Skill, and Stripe included. PowerPoint remained uncertain within the schedule, and website and GTM work would begin after release.

title: US go-to-market execution remains unclear
content: The team identified unclear US go-to-market execution, especially the target, message, and channels, as its largest business risk.

title: Workspace production stability is uncertain
content: The team raised concerns about concurrent Workspace users, server capacity, error response, and session routing in production.

title: Split the first implementation between UX and technical research
content: Sangyeon will design the UX and stabilize Word evaluation. Changshik will research cloud versus local execution, agent and database placement, email and calendar CRUD and synchronization, meeting transcription, and memory architecture.

title: Target July 31 for the client-workflow product milestone
content: The project plan targets completion by July 31, with the first week devoted to product planning, UX design, Word stabilization, and technical research.

title: Implement the meeting-to-project workflow first
content: The first representative workflow should capture an offline meeting, summarize it, find an existing related project or propose creating one, create follow-up todos, draft a follow-up email, and add calendar work. A later incoming email should find the project, update existing work, and start the next cycle.

title: Integrate Gmail and Outlook instead of operating an email server
content: The product will read and synchronize inbox data through Gmail and Outlook integrations rather than operate its own email server.

title: Target professionals who manage client-centered work
content: The product concept is an end-to-end AI workflow system for professionals who manage multiple clients or cases, hold frequent meetings, exchange emails and documents, and earn money from document-based outputs. Candidate users include lawyers, patent attorneys, salespeople, and consultants.

title: Trigger workflows from incoming email and calendar events
content: The product workflow should start automatically from external events such as incoming email and calendar activity, instead of requiring every workflow to begin with a manual prompt.

title: A generic agent without user-specific context will not be differentiated
content: The team expects users to reject an agent that feels like generic GPT output. The product needs to learn each professional's patterns, frameworks, project history, and intent so its actions and drafts feel grounded in the user's actual way of working.

title: Cloud versus local architecture remained unresolved
content: The team did not finalize whether the product should be local or cloud-based. It agreed that the agent and its database should live in the same environment, noted that local storage creates future migration and multi-device problems, and determined that UX design can continue while the technical architecture is researched.

title: Maintain chronological short memory plus project context
content: The proposed agent memory design keeps a chronological short memory of actions such as meetings and sent emails while maintaining shared project context. Recent events could be capped at roughly 50-100 entries, with older context fetched on demand and skills and tools loaded lazily; the exact limit was not finalized.

title: Transcribe completed meeting recordings with Whisper and diarization
content: The proposed meeting-note pipeline uses Whisper with speaker diarization. Processing the recording after the meeting was considered more useful than showing a live transcript, although the implementation approach still required technical research.

title: Use planning, worker, and editing agents with human-in-the-loop control
content: A three-layer architecture was proposed: a planning agent determines the next work, worker agents perform actions such as email, project, issue, calendar, web, and document generation, and an editing agent handles document edits. Preview-and-action interactions and human approval would preserve control instead of making the system fully autonomous.

title: Recruit 20 workflow interview participants from inline AI users
content: The team will request interviews from inline AI's 28,000 members and recruit 20 working professionals who rely heavily on email, manage clients, take meeting notes, and perform follow-up work; students are excluded.

title: Research markets before selecting strategy and product
content: The team will research candidate markets using Market Attractiveness, Sector Landscape, Workflow Landscape, and Competitive Landscape, then select a market, define the ICP and competitive positioning, and only then plan the product.

title: Stabilize document conversion and validate skills on real files
content: The team will investigate a more stable LibreOffice conversion path and validate document-generation skills against its existing test files, aiming for a diverse set of roughly 50 to 100 files rather than judging only a few examples.

title: Choose a domain before planning the next product
content: The team concluded that the vague AI OS idea space was too difficult to express and pursue without strong conviction, and decided to select a specific domain and market before defining product strategy and entering product planning.

title: The support flow made technical problems hard to communicate
content: A customer had already tried email and KakaoTalk before calling, but the team still struggled to identify the exact failure. The customer remained polite but was frustrated enough to call directly, exposing a weakness in issue intake and communication.

title: PDF-to-Word conversion quality remains limited
content: The team acknowledged that PDF-to-Word conversion quality remains limited and still needs validation across diverse source files.

title: PowerPoint files shrink during processing
content: PowerPoint files were repeatedly shrinking during processing, and the team had not confirmed a solution.

title: The company lacks a stable target market and decision criteria
content: The team diagnosed the core business problem as having no clear target market, insufficient market and customer understanding, no stable strategy, and decisions that repeatedly change because they are based on internal arguments rather than external evidence and explicit criteria.

title: A long-document failure led to an immediate refund
content: A customer reported that processing a document of several hundred pages stalled and consumed the available credits. The team understood the failure during a phone call and immediately refunded the June 19 payment.

title: Legal and sales are the initial market candidates
content: The initial candidate markets listed for domain research were legal services and sales.

title: Monthly service usage increased from 3,900 to 4,400 users
content: The team reported approximately 3,900 users two months earlier and 4,400 users in the previous month.

title: Begin overseas direct investment reporting
content: 이상연 will contact 신한 to begin the overseas direct investment reporting process.

title: Close the Barbarossa format-conversion loop by July 20
content: The team will share the Barbarossa format-conversion results by July 20 and then mark the work complete instead of allowing the evaluation loop to continue indefinitely.

title: Complete all code-based document-generation skills by July 22
content: The team will finish the PDF, Excel, DOCX, PPTX, and HWPX creator skills by July 22, adapting Anthropic's skill instructions and tools to the inline AI environment and completing the HWPX creator beyond its draft state.

title: Finish file reading, Stripe, and Workspace infrastructure this week
content: The team will add support for reading all file types during the current week and finish Stripe integration and Workspace infrastructure by July 23.

title: Implement multi-agent editing UX and Search Chat
content: Starting July 23, the team will implement format-specific edit windows, multiple windows and agents, session reload behavior, document-window routing and notifications, and Search Chat, targeting completion of this UX work by July 24.

title: Move editing instructions from skills into tool descriptions
content: The team will remove proprietary editing tags from inline skills, migrate the instructions into tool descriptions, and verify whether legacy edit-tool deserialization and compaction logic can be disabled without breaking old sessions.

title: Seek remediation for the rejected Mercury application
content: The team will continue asking Mercury which supplementary documents could improve the rejected account application; Mercury's policy does not disclose the rejection reason.

title: Build a capture-to-document loop around meetings
content: The product concept is Turn your meetings into complete documents: a meeting should be captured, matched to an appropriate document format, and turned into a completed deliverable. Meeting notes and the post-meeting format suggestion are required parts of the Version 1 scope, not optional add-ons.

title: Finish the document foundation before entering US GTM
content: The confirmed direction is to finish Word, code-based document generation, Stripe, reusable script automation through Skill and simple UX, and meeting notes before beginning US go-to-market work.

title: Run Barbarossa QA on July 27 and target release on August 7
content: The team set July 27 for the Barbarossa QA review and August 7 as the final release target, with meeting-note and document-automation development starting after the current foundation work.

title: Add reusable design themes to generated documents
content: The team proposed a design.md layer that describes fonts, colors, layouts, and other rules, plus predefined code-importable themes that apply defaults to headings and paragraphs while allowing property overrides. The style-property foundation should be built first, and the theme layer should be decided after Terra and Luna tests.

title: Evaluate meeting-note transcription with cloud-stored audio
content: The proposed meeting-note architecture stores recordings and transcripts in the cloud, runs evaluation on the backend, and compares ElevenLabs with OpenAI Whisper using a small evaluation set with both Korean and English recordings. Speaker diarization and prompt limitations still need verification.

title: Raw XML outperformed CVD in document-editing evaluation
content: The July 18 evaluation found equal cost between raw XML and CVD editing, with XML becoming cheaper on larger documents. Value reflection favored XML at 76.7% versus 70.3% for HWP and 95.7% versus 91.3% for Word, but XML could silently delete tables or cells and had about 2.5 times the Bash-command failure rate, so safeguards are still required.

title: Interview 20 US lawyers and 10 Korean lawyers before finalizing direction
content: The team will interview 20 lawyers in the United States and 10 lawyers in Korea, and will avoid treating the legal direction as final until all 30 interviews supply enough evidence for a decision.

title: Ship the current Word, document-generation, Stripe, and UX build
content: The team will ship the current build with Word, document generation, Stripe integration, and the planned UX while the lawyer interviews and legal-domain validation proceed.

title: Keep the legal pivot inside inline AI instead of forking a new service
content: The current decision is to pursue the legal-domain direction within the existing inline AI product rather than split off a separate service, avoiding duplicate infrastructure, back-office, administration, team setup, and Stripe operations.

title: Prioritize the US and stop prioritizing Korea-specific features
content: The team aligned on the United States as the first-priority market and decided that new product work should no longer prioritize HWP or other Korea- and Korean-language-specific capabilities.

title: Product direction keeps changing without new evidence
content: The team traced repeated uncertainty to a mismatch between the stated US goal and continued work on Korea-specific features, plus a pattern of making verbal decisions without supplying the interviews or data needed to keep those decisions stable.

title: Test an AI OS for one-to-ten-person law firms
content: The provisional product direction is a legal-domain AI OS for one-to-ten-person law firms in Korea and the United States, covering legal search, document automation, meeting notes, email, and large PDFs. The direction remains subject to validation rather than being a permanent market commitment.

title: Investment due diligence completed without issues
content: The team received confirmation that the investment due-diligence process was completed without problems after the requested materials were prepared.

title: Deploy the current product this week before choosing the next direction
content: The team plans to deploy what has already been built during the current week. After deployment, it will operate the product, begin looking for acquisition opportunities, and select and deeply investigate the next product direction.

title: A pivot away from inline AI means narrowing the customer and restarting
content: The team aligned that pivoting away from inline AI means selecting one target customer and being willing to start from zero, including the service form, customer, product narrative, and implementation rather than treating the pivot as a small feature change.

title: Choose a large market and understand one differentiated segment deeply
content: Sunwoo Seunghwan advised that the company must participate in a large market, deliver a differentiated user experience within a specific segment, and be able to explain the target customer and market in depth; a strong product in a small market may still fail to grow.

title: U.S. legal and knowledge-worker directions require deeper validation
content: Open questions include whether meaningful U.S. legal-market share remains after broad Harvey adoption by AmLaw 100 firms, whether smaller firms have adequate willingness to pay, whether a Korean team can execute U.S. legal go-to-market efficiently, and whether workflow redesign for high-context-switching knowledge workers is a real pain rather than a tarpit already addressed with coding agents.

title: inline AI lacked a clearly defined end goal
content: The stated reason for pivoting before another release was that the product had no clearly defined endpoint or target outcome, making the direction ambiguous.

title: Four product directions remained under consideration after deployment
content: The unresolved directions were to investigate the U.S. legal market deeply, redesign knowledge-worker workflows around AI, continue with a document-generation API, or continue building an agent for Korean public-sector customers. No final direction was selected in this meeting.

title: Attempt real sales and user discovery during the remaining SF stay
content: During the roughly two remaining weeks in San Francisco, the team will pitch and try to sell the product to real users, conduct coffee chats with roles such as accountants and product managers, and combine those sales loops with case-study research.

title: Build a proactive to-do app demo before the Monday pitch
content: The team will create a proactive to-do app demo for the Monday pitch. The concept is to infer, create, and schedule tasks from context instead of requiring the user to enter every task manually.

title: Port inline AI to macOS and verify Apple Developer signing
content: The team will port the existing Windows Electron wrapper for inline AI to macOS, begin from the six core files in the AI-Agent folder, and verify whether the Apple Developer signing certificate is still valid or must be renewed.

title: Prioritize SF practitioner networking events over hackathons
content: The team will review the San Francisco event list together and prioritize practitioner networking events such as founder breakfasts, builder breakfasts, and GTM gatherings over spending most of the remaining stay at hackathons.

title: Review the Korea-versus-United-States direction every week
content: The team will hold a recurring weekly discussion about whether the company should operate from Korea or the United States until the decision and its rationale are aligned.

title: Use the SF stay to learn target selection through real market experience
content: The purpose of the remaining San Francisco stay was defined as learning a repeatable framework for choosing a target user and problem, then testing that framework through interviews, sales attempts, and case studies rather than relying on abstract discussion.

title: inline AI was assessed as a vulnerable frontier-model wrapper
content: The team assessed the current inline AI structure as closer to a search or distribution layer over frontier models, leaving it exposed when Claude, OpenAI, or another frontier lab expands into the same application layer. They believed a defensible AI application would need to own a specific domain's workflow and ecosystem.

title: The Korea-versus-United-States business location remained unresolved
content: The team did not decide whether to build the business in Korea or the United States. They agreed that either choice required a clear, memorable rationale grounded in experience because choosing only by market size or familiarity would cause the decision to be reopened later.

title: Explore deep enterprise AI adoption support as a Korea-focused direction
content: One proposed direction was to help enterprises adopt AI by deeply understanding a company's domain workflow and removing deployment barriers without becoming a conventional SI vendor. Pharmaceutical and biotech workflows were discussed as possible examples, but the direction was not approved.

title: Explore technically difficult products outside frontier-lab application territory
content: Another unapproved direction was to use AI to build software that remains technically difficult and is less exposed to frontier-lab competition, with indie games, an operating system for agents, and a browser discussed as examples.
